author: WP14
summary: Alpha.1-era media chapter: Song contract, MediaLibrary metadata, queue and playback, visualization, video contract, platform limits. Largely current in substance, but the video platform story (link-time failure, Windows guard defect) is obsolete, Opus is not decodable, the visualization normalization and test claims are wrong, and a video-track switch always recreates the texture. Media internals and the FFmpeg page already held the scan, queue and decoder internals; a new public-contract deep dive holds the rest.

concepts.text: Media is no longer a shell-heavy namespace: it holds file-backed songs and libraries, playlist parsing, queued playback, visualization data, picture libraries and FFmpeg video where enabled.
tokens: no longer the thin shell older counts described

concepts.text: The chapter states behaviours by subsystem instead of replacing the README's test count with another undated total.
concepts.note: Book methodology about avoiding undated counts; no TARGET fact to carry.

concepts.text: Audio and Media form an intentional static-library cycle: FrameworkDispatcher in Audio advances MediaPlayer while Media sends song playback to the audio mixer.
tokens: depend on each other on purpose

concepts.text: CMake repeats the archives to resolve the cycle; removing either edge would require reassigning the shared dispatcher and playback responsibilities.
tokens: Removing either edge would mean moving the dispatcher

concepts.text: A Song can be constructed from a path or discovered by a MediaLibrary scan.
A directly constructed song has null, non-owning Album, Artist and Genre links; a scan supplies them from the library hierarchy.

concepts.text: FNA's Song omits Album, Artist, Genre and ToString() from the XNA 4.0 surface; FNA-only reviews missed this and a comparison with recorded XNA 4.0 API data found it.

concepts.text: API parity with FNA and with XNA are separate claims.
The ContentManager song reader advertises .aac and .wma, which the vendored mixer cannot decode; the MediaLibrary scanner omits them.
A loose-file resolution match establishes that a Song can name the file, not that the mixer can decode it.

concepts.text: Claim that MP3, Ogg, WAV, FLAC and Opus follow the installed decoder routes: Opus is not decodable at TARGET (SDL3_mixer Opus off, CNA's mixer refuses Ogg Opus), although both the song reader and the library scan accept .opus.

concepts.note: Opus removed from the playable list; issue CNA-BUG-052 still present.

concepts.text: MediaLibrary scans the host music and picture directories returned by SDL_GetUserFolder.
concepts.note: Roots come from the platform filesystem service: SDL on SDL3, known folders on Win32, XDG elsewhere.

concepts.note: The override is internal (CNA::Internal::Media::MediaLibraryPaths), not a public CNAEXT member.

concepts.text: The library builds SongCollection, Album, Artist and Genre relationships plus the parallel picture hierarchy.
SavePicture() creates a Saved Pictures node on first use.
tokens: Merely constructing or browsing a library never creates Saved Pictures

concepts.text: The in-tree tag parser reads Ogg Vorbis comments and Ogg Opus OpusTags.
It reads ID3v2.3/2.4 title, artist, album, genre, track, rating and picture frames.
ID3 text may be Latin-1, UTF-16 with BOM, UTF-16BE or UTF-8.
Native FLAC VORBIS_COMMENT and picture blocks are read.
.m3u and .m3u8 playlists are read as UTF-8.
Files without readable tags fall back to file name, parent and grandparent directory for title, album and artist.
Missing playlist entries are skipped.
Album art comes from cover.jpg/folder.jpg or embedded ID3/FLAC pictures; the front-cover picture type wins when present.
tokens: folder art wins over embedded art
concepts.note: Folder images (cover, folder, front, album, albumart; jpg/jpeg/png) win over embedded art at TARGET; front-cover preference among embedded pictures not re-checked.

concepts.text: Mapping ID3's 0-255 rating and informal Vorbis scales to XNA's 0-10 property is CNA policy, not an XNA rule.
Scans are synchronous snapshots; there is no MediaLibrary::Refresh().
The tag parser once read TRCK correctly while MediaLibrary dropped it when building Song; only a fixture checked after library construction exposed it.
MediaPlayer supplies song and collection playback, pause, resume, stop, shuffle, repeat, queue navigation, events and visualization.
Playlist is read-only, as in XNA.
MediaQueue::Add(Song*) adopts its pointer whereas SongCollection is non-owning.
To keep the queue from deleting library-owned songs, MediaPlayer::Play clones each input song and enqueues the clone.
In linear mode next and previous clamp at the ends unless repeat is enabled; with repeat the end wraps to the beginning.
tokens: repeat at the last index wraps to zero

concepts.text: Shuffle chooses uniformly from the full queue, so a track may repeat immediately.
Sound-enabled builds use SDL3_mixer's stopped callback to advance.
concepts.note: The stopped callback is the selected mixer's (SDL3_mixer or CNA's own mixer under ALSA).

concepts.text: The no-sound fallback compares elapsed time with a known nonzero duration; a zero-duration song does not auto-advance.
tokens: a song never auto-advances or ends on its own
concepts.note: Queued copies never carry a duration and the mixer-less path never sets one, so in SDL2/NULL builds no song auto-advances at all.

concepts.text: Volume and mute are independent state: setting volume while muted keeps the value for the next unmute and only the mixer receives zero gain while muted.
tokens: setting the volume while muted stores the new value

concepts.text: MediaStateChanged and ActiveSongChanged are deferred until FrameworkDispatcher::Update().
tokens: are never raised from the mixer callback

concepts.text: Game calls the dispatcher during its update loop, but code using the static media API outside Game must pump it explicitly.
tokens: a derived Update that never calls the base class

concepts.text: GetVisualizationData() consumes samples captured by the mixer's post-mix callback.
concepts.note: Post-mix callback of the selected mixer, not only SDL3_mixer.

concepts.text: The callback writes a single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer without allocation, locking or exceptions.
tokens: must not allocate, lock or throw

concepts.text: Sample slots are std::atomic<float> with relaxed ordering so audio-thread writes and game-thread reads are defined behaviour.
A reader may observe samples spanning adjacent callback batches; the one-frame visual imprecision is accepted.
A 512-sample Hann-windowed radix-2 FFT produces XNA's 256 bins.

Claim that CNA scales a full-amplitude sine to about 1.0 in its bin: magnitudes are scaled by 2/N with the Hann window's coherent gain of one half left uncompensated, so the peak is near 0.5 by that arithmetic (the source comment says about 1.0); XNA documented no normalization.
Disabled or not-yet-fed visualization returns zero-filled arrays.

Claim that tests cover failed installation and removal of the mixer tap: the enabled flag is assigned only from what happened, but the media tests always have a working dummy-driver mixer, so the failed-install branch is correct by construction and not by test.
tokens: correct by construction rather than by test
concepts.note: The test comment itself disclaims coverage of the failed-install branch.

concepts.text: The CMake configuration disables FFmpeg on Windows (MinGW and MSVC), Android and Emscripten.
concepts.note: iOS is excluded too, and CNA_ENABLE_VIDEO=ON is a configure error there.

concepts.text: Native-Windows guard mismatch: CMake's unavailable set includes WIN32 but two ContentManager.cpp guards check Emscripten, Android and MinGW (MinGW twice) and not _WIN32.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: ContentManager.cpp includes Media/Video/Video.hpp unconditionally and has no video preprocessor guard; Video and VideoPlayer are always compiled with VideoDecoderUnavailable.cpp as fallback. CNA-BUG-051 reading: absent.

concepts.text: An MSVC build could therefore retain Video dispatch references after the implementations were excluded: an open build defect at the Bible's pin.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the implementations are no longer excluded on any target, so the dangling-reference link failure cannot occur; the video status line reports NotSupportedException instead.
